NO MCQs anywhere, so every row is subjective with no answer field and there is no Section-A key table to read. INTERNAL CHOICE - DISAGREEMENT WITH THE BRIEF, CONFIRMED: this paper prints only SIX general instructions and NOT ONE of them mentions internal choice or gives a count (TRANSCRIPTION_BRIEF section 5 says the count is instruction (vi) on a 2022 term2 paper; here (vi) is 'Use of log tables and calculators is not allowed'), yet FIVE internal choices exist: Q4, Q5, Q9, Q11 and Q12(iv). NOTATION: the molar-conductivity symbol prints as a wedge-like glyph with subscript m; it is capital lambda and is transcribed \Lambda_{\mathrm{m}}, matching the sibling papers. The standard-potential symbol is a CIRCLED MINUS superscript, not a degree sign, transcribed ^{\ominus} - same as 56/2/1. The crystal-field splitting subscript in Q5(a)(i) is a lowercase letter o (checked enlarged), transcribed \Delta_{\mathrm{o}}. Single quotes around compound labels 'A', 'B', 'C' print curly and are transcribed as ASCII, matching the siblings. CBSE-VOIDED QUESTIONS: NONE. All six marking-scheme pages were read end to end and neither 'Full mark to be awarded for any option' nor 'Award full mark if attempted' nor any equivalent appears anywhere; the only marking accommodations are '(or any other suitable method of conversion)', '(Any two)', '(Any three correct reactions)', '(or any other correct reaction)' and '(Deduct 1/2 marks for no or incorrect unit)', none of which voids a question. OUTDATED CHAPTER: exactly ONE question is Surface Chemistry - Q8, the Freundlich adsorption isotherm plot - filed on 'Surface Chemistry [Outdated]' / 'Adsorption'. Found by content, not by carrying over a question number from another set. No question fell outside the ten live chapters plus Surface Chemistry, so no _outOfSyllabus flag was needed. FIGURES: two, both REQUIRED - Q8's log(x/m) vs log p plot and Q11(b)'s enthalpy-of-atomisation graph. No drawn organic structures anywhere on this paper: every compound is named in words or given as a formula, so nothing needed describing-rather-than-naming. DEFECTS: none that changes an answer. questions.subtopic: Factors Influencing Rate of a Reaction
questions.context: The rate law for a chemical reaction relates the reaction rate with the concentrations or partial pressures of the reactants. For a general reaction aA + bB \(\rightarrow\) C with no intermediate steps in its reaction mechanism, meaning that it is an elementary reaction, the rate law is given by \(r = k[\mathrm{A}]^{x}[\mathrm{B}]^{y}\), where [A] and [B] express the concentrations of A and B in moles per litre. Exponents x and y vary for each reaction and are determined experimentally. The value of k varies with conditions that affect reaction rate, such as temperature, pressure, surface area, etc. The sum of these exponents is known as overall reaction order. A zero order reaction has a constant rate that is independent of the concentration of the reactants. A first order reaction depends on the concentration of only one reactant. A reaction is said to be second order when the overall order is two. Once we have determined the order of the reaction, we can go back and plug in one set of our initial values and solve for k.
questions.stem:
Calculate the overall order of a reaction which has the following rate expression :
\(\text{Rate} = k[\mathrm{A}]^{1/2}\,[\mathrm{B}]^{3/2}\)
